# govulncheck baseline — vulnerabilities this codebase's call graph can REACH today.
#
# This file is the gate. .github/workflows/govulncheck.yml fails when a scan
# finds a called-level vulnerability that is NOT listed here. Pre-existing
# findings do not fail the build; a NEW one does.
#
# That is deliberate. Flipping straight to "fail on any finding" with 24 open
# would have failed every PR for problems unrelated to its diff, and a check
# that is always red is a check nobody reads. A report-only job has the
# opposite failure: it is always green, so the only signal is a job summary
# nobody opens on a green run. The ratchet is the version that actually bites:
# it cannot go up silently.
#
# WHEN A SCAN FAILS: a new vulnerability became reachable. Fix it if you can
# (bump the dependency, bump the toolchain, stop calling the vulnerable path).
# Only add an ID here if it genuinely cannot be fixed right now, and write the
# reason on the line above it. An entry with no justification is a bug.
#
# WHEN THE COUNT DROPS: the job says so and asks you to delete the cleared
# lines. It does not fail — a shrinking list is the point — but leaving stale
# entries lets a fixed vulnerability silently come back.
#
# Format: one GO-XXXX-NNNN per line. `#` comments and blank lines ignored.
#
# Baseline captured 2026-08-21 against main (24 findings). The 20 Go standard
# library entries were cleared on 2026-10-07 by bumping go.mod to go 1.25.14;
# every one was fixed in a 1.25.x patch release (1.25.9 through 1.25.13).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# github.com/hamba/avro/v2 (3 findings) — UNFIXABLE, tracked in #2817
#
# All three are decoder-side (CPU exhaustion, integer overflow, unbounded map
# allocation) and all are "Fixed in: N/A". Upstream ARCHIVED the repository on
# 2026-01-18; v2.31.0 is final. Reached via conduit-commons/schema/avro from
# the built-in Avro processor, so this is data-path code decoding untrusted
# input. #2817 tracks the decision: fork, replace the codec, bound the input at
# the call site, or accept and document. Do not remove these lines until that
# issue is resolved — they are the reason the issue exists.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CPU exhaustion in Avro decoder in github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 and github.com/hamba/avro/v2
GO-2026-5046
# Integer overflow in Avro decoder in github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 and github.com/hamba/avro/v2
GO-2026-5047
# Denial of service via unbounded map allocations in github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 and github.com/hamba/avro/v2
GO-2026-5048

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# golang.org/x/crypto (1 finding)
#
# The openpgp package is unmaintained and "unsafe by design" per its own
# advisory — there is no fixed version, only "stop using it." Indirect; needs
# tracing to whichever dependency pulls it in before it can be dropped.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package is unmaintained, unsafe by design, and has known security issues
GO-2026-5932
